text:
The Flames' biggest headline of the month was a loss off the scoresheet: Kevin Bahl's season-ending injury. He and Simon Nemec had been Calgary's most even pair on chances, and now the blue line is leaning harder on Jake Middleton and Zach Whitecloud, who have been outscored 11-8 together, and on the club's AHL depth.

The happier stories are Zayne Parekh, whose breakout has the hockey world asking how good he already is, and goalie Devin Cooley, profiled in The New Yorker for the way he thinks about the position. Joel Farabee has also given Calgary some finish after a slow start on breakaways.

The trouble is scoring. Calgary averages 2.48 goals a game and gets only 45% of the expected goals, our measure of chance quality, so this is not just bad luck. The power play generates very little, and Matt Coronato has 2 points in his last 10 games against 7.4 expected from his chances, a cold run that should ease if he keeps getting looks.

At 10-12-1, the Flames have about the points their play has earned, and our playoff odds sit at 9% after Thursday's 4-1 loss to Minnesota. What we'd watch under Ryan Huska: whether Parekh's minutes keep climbing, because right now he looks like the most dangerous thing they have.
headline: Calgary's defense lost a pillar and its offense lost its touch
